name: Early-onset Posterior Polar Cataract

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Slit-lamp Diagnostic Criteria for Posterior Polar Cataract

criteria.description: Presence of a well-demarcated, round or oval opacity at the posterior pole of the lens
Visual impairment manifesting in early childhood or adolescence
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy confirming posterior polar lens opacity without anterior segment abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of posterior polar lens opacity confirmed by slit-lamp examination with early-onset visual impairment; family history supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis but is not routinely required.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic sharply demarcated opacity at the posterior pole of the lens.
searchTerms: cloudy spot at back center of lens

pathognomonic.notes: Visual impairment typically presenting in childhood or adolescence.

common.notes: Increased sensitivity to bright light due to lens opacity.
Impaired accommodation related to lens opacity.
Both eyes commonly affected, though severity may differ.
Opacity may increase in density over time.

occasional.notes: Involuntary eye movements secondary to early visual deprivation.
Misalignment of the eyes due to impaired binocular vision.
Reduced vision in one eye due to abnormal visual development.
Perception of flashes of light occasionally reported.

rare.notes: Partial displacement of the lens may rarely occur.
Elevated intraocular pressure as a complication.
Increased risk due to fragile posterior capsule.

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing sharply demarcated posterior polar lens opacity
Ultrasound biomicroscopy may be used to assess posterior capsule integrity
genetic: Mutations in the PITX3 gene associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Visual acuity testing showing decreased vision

distinguishingFeatures: Opacity located in the central nucleus rather than posterior pole
Opacity beneath the posterior capsule but more diffuse and less sharply demarcated
Often associated with steroid use or radiation exposure
Later onset compared to posterior polar cataract

redFlags: Rapid progression of lens opacity causing sudden vision loss
Signs of secondary glaucoma such as eye pain and redness
Posterior capsule rupture risk during cataract surgery
references: Shiels A, Hejtmancik JF. Genetic origins of cataract. Arch Ophthalmol. 2007;125(2):165-173.
Orphanet: Early-onset posterior polar cataract - ORPHA:98993
